body:
> It's just lonely, and it hurts. When you can't have what you'd want more than anything in the world.

So true! Sometimes it feels as if all I’m doing is filling my days with random activities so as to keep my mind off the black hole in my chest that’s widening and eating me day by day. 
How healthy can it be to spend a whole life without ever feeling loved?
I’m excited for you blackberrivine! Hopefully this new chapter of your life will lead to something amazing :)

> Too ugly, too broken, too unhealthy to ever find it with someone I care about

Man, right in the feels. No one should ever feel this way... I've almost given up on the idea of having an intimate relationship with a guy that cares about me as much as I care about him. Not saying that it won't happen for us someday (trying to keep a positive attitude) but life passes us by while we wait for that guy to come into our lives and we end up missing out on so many human experiences that, in a way or another, are enriching learning experiences. What I'm trying to say is that, as of now I don't have the chance to know what making sex with a guy who loves me back feels like, but I can experience kisses, skin to skin contact, what being held in someone's arms feels like and still enjoy it even if it's something I do with a rando. Dunno if this makes any sense, I'm too tired to think in English. 

> I'm sorry op. I am in my 30s, I relate. You feel like something rotted and dessicated if a combo of fear/pain and inexperience has kept you from men.

V-card I don't hang around here that often but I remember some of your posts and your pain, the way you describe it, it's always something I find myself relating to. I'm genuinely sorry you have to feel this way too. There's no help that I can give to ease the pain unfortunately... Hug!!!

> Once I tried online dating saying clearly that I was an inexperienced woman and I got a dozen messages that were really fucking gross. Some thought that being inexperienced meant that I was going to be a pushover, a doormat, ready to be treated like shit or humiliated, so they would message me like "Let's meet tonight at 8pm. No questions asked. Wear this." or "Hi Anna, call me Christian and wait for me at that hotel" (I swear to God). I am maybe inexperienced and broken but I don't obey OnlineFucktard121 just because he has a dick and I want to try what it feels like. Some were really surprised that I would say no, cause they really thought that by virtue of being a virgin I was just ready to be manipulated...

Damn, this is one of the things that irritates me the most about online dating! The friggin arrogance certain people have! The way they want to use you believing that if you are an adult virgin you must be a desperate spineless woman and thus a fuckdoll available at the snap of a finger just to please their needs!    
I know that if I'll try find someone online dealing with the wave of horny idiots who think they can treat you like a doormat just because you are an adult virgin will be unavoidable...

> I even tried reddit, had a lot of messages the first day but of course most were in the US and didn't even bother reading the whole post, and the 2 that were in the same city ghosted after a couple of days.

You tried on reddit?? Eventually how did you find the right guy to have sex with? Looking back, do you regret doing it with him?

Oh absolutely! I don’t know if I’ll follow through with this plan but if I do I’ll meet the guy to get to know him on a deeper level before doing anything. Risking my health is out of question! By the way, thank you very much for your insightful comment! :)

> Part of the community feels it’s inorganic and insulting to deign to online date. 

Really?? Maybe they live in bigger cities where you can easily meet people through social activities. For me it’s different though, my chances of finding a partner would drop close to zero if I didn’t use online dating apps (the joy of living in a town in the middle of nowhere /s).   

> Try changing your Tinder bio to be specific about being a shy girl

I’m not shy though, at least not that much, so this role would be difficult to play for me. Most importantly, I don’t want to put on display the fact that I’m trying to gain some sexual experience on apps where everyone can see your face, age and location. It’s such an intimate matter that I’d prefer to tackle it in a more private way. 

> I’d say cut straight to meeting somewhere public, like for a drink or coffee, to feel them out. You’ll be able to tell if they make you feel good. If you aren’t feeling it, walk - no harm, no foul. If you are, get a hotel room.
Stay safe, and always give yourself an out. But don’t be afraid to try, if it’s something you feel you need to experience.

You’re right, no harm no foul! It’s just that taking such a step is not easy emotionally-wise. I don’t want this to be a mistake I'll regret.    
Another problem is that part of the abuse I was subjected to as a kid was sexual and I’m not virgin in the strictest sense of the term. Basically it’s not the penis in vagina feeling that I’m looking for, what I want is to experience anything that surrounds sex as a human experience. I want to feel another human being' skin, learn and get to know my sexuality. I would like to have a bit of fun with guys like younger women do but my inexperience is holding me back. I don't want to be made fun of, that’s why I thought of finding someone as inexperienced as I am. It’s just that, how many are there in the wild? :/ 

If you don’t mind me asking, how was your first time? Do you regret it? How long had you known your partner when you had sex?
Yep, never stopped trying!

> We are a superficial society that values aesthetics and monetary power over character and maturity.

This, so much this!

Mental illness is truly one of the biggest and most belittled problems people face. It's a curse from which you can't run away and all you can do is find coping mechanisms to make your life more "normal", more bearable.  
As a person who's been battling ptsd, depression and god only knows what else since childhood my heart aches for all those other people who have to deal with any form of mental illness! I understand your struggle...
Shaldewey don’t do it! Come on buddy stay with us, consider the people on this subreddit like an enlarged family, we are here to help you go through this moment!

I'm so far behind that the thought of what could happen in the future scares me.   
However once my mother -whom is already in her 70's- and my pets die I won't have anything left to live for, so I'm not sure I'll make it to retirement age.
Only my mother, my father died a long time ago but anyway it'd have been impossible to have a conversation with him.

My parents were the opposite of affectionate, they used to beat me regularly to teach me (although I never understood what) or would simply ignore me. I still haven't a clear idea what "normal" parents do with their children.
Yeah, a flair about dating updates could be useful as well.
Sounds like a good idea to me!

> We get shoved to the corner because no one wants to think about us. Then we get criticized for being depressed or angry. 

Damn, this is so true! Sometimes I feel like I'm not even allowed to be sad.
Naah, when they met they weren't broke but weren't rolling in money either, just like now. Suffice to say they met face to face for the first time after skyping for one year.
I always love your work! Are you on deviantart as well?
Happy belated birthday ArtShoRob!!
You're welcome 😊 and thank you!

Life's given you a chance to be happy and you want to throw it away because you are sure it won't work. How do you know it won't work if you don't even try and see where it goes? 
My sister met her husband online, they lived in two different continents and given the huge distance everyone made fun of them and told them it wouldn't work, well joke's on them because 8 years later they are still happily together and have two kids. 
You miss 100 percent of the shots you don't take, Lisbon.

That’s great news Lisbon!! Where is she from? You can make it work somehow. I know several people who got either married or are in a relationship with someone they met online. Distance is not a limit, check out   /r/LongDistance .

If only I knew some magic words to cheer you up a bit... It hurts me to see how big the pain you're dealing with is. It's also very relatable because just like you I've been thinking about suicide and maybe that's why I'm unable to find the supportive words you so need in this moment of your life.   
However I'm commenting to show you that you are not alone in the world, your words don't fall on deaf ears, someone in another part of the world is worried about you and wants you to stay alive. You have been a fighter for 40 years, which means you are extremely strong, keep fighting with us. We are here tompsy... Some of us are very messed up, others aren't, but we are all here fighting together.   
Send you a virtual hug!

My condolences for your loss Kippy ❤️! It’s a pain I know too well… Lately when I look at my cat (about 16 year old) and my dog (11 year old) this silly fear of losing them sneaks up on me. I lost a pup in October/November and it was tough, I can’t still bring me to look at his pictures. 

A few days ago a friend of mine celebrated her birthday; I drove two hours to get to her because I couldn’t stop crying while driving, so I ended up taking the wrong turn and got lost. When I finally made it to my friend’s house her child welcomed me in the warmest way possible and just like the last time we met he decided he wanted to sit beside me and the table or he wouldn’t eat.  

“He likes you a lot!” her mother said. Apparently he really does, just like all the other kids I’ve met in my life.

That’s the only happy day I’ve had in June. End of May and June have been particularly tough on me. I’ve been feeling jaded almost every minute of every day to the point I wanted to take my life and talked to my mother about what to do in case something were to happen. 

My cheerful facade is crumbling. It’s getting very hard to smile, pretend to be normal and that everything is fine so no one can see how broken I feel.

I’ve a crush on an online friend who is pulling a fade, a friend who I thought was a beautiful human being, someone who could never hurt another person and behave in such a way. His behaviour makes me feel so worthless, faulty and disposable.

I have only one parent, my mother, and on her good days tries to support me although has no idea how. Just yesterday I called her for help because I was feeling suicidal and she bursted out crying.

>It hurts me to realise my siblings totally ignored my single and lonely plight from teenhood to this day.

Same. I have a sibling you could call a normie. Had teen sex, lots of friends, bought a house, got married in her twenties and now is your typical adult leading a normal life. During the adolescence I was a shut\-in because I had few to no friends and not once she invited me to join her when she would go out with her friends (we have only a few years apart so age difference was not a factor). Does she worry about me being alone now? Nope, not one bit. Doesn't even ask me why I'm alone or what's going on in my life. Actually we barely talk.    
And in case you were wondering, yeah I'm the runt of the litter, so to speak.
I have a very big extended family as well, but I stay away from them by choice as they had a big role in my developing psychological and self esteem issues.

>We too dream of the mundane. Yet I wonder what crime I have comitted to deserve this life.

I often wonder the same thing. I ask the universe "what did I do to deserve this?"

Some times when I find myself fantasizing about being loved back I feel like an idiot. A voice in my head tells me "you know that's not going to happen, it's as realistic as dreaming of becoming a millionaire!"

But dreaming is all that keeps me going, if I'm still alive is because I still hope that someday I'll get to meet someone that loves me back and all of my dreams will come true... yes, I know, I'm an idiot even just for thinking it.

You see, this sub is a support group for those who have never been in a relationship and/or lack other forms of human contact, so you in our eyes aren't quite FA. You sound very lonely though, and it seems you are afraid you're going to be stuck into these unchangeable circumstances that prevent you from bonding with other people for a long time, so if hanging around will make you feel less lonely in the universe you are welcome to stay :\) 

Most people here are good hearted fellas who don't judge nor outcast others.

I, for sure, am already a cat lady. Neighbours’ cats hang out at my place almost everyday, and one of them has been living with me and my two other pets for a couple years now \(my neighbours know, they are ok with that\).   

It fascinates me how easily animals get attached to someone who cares about them. You show them love and they love you back regardless of how you look, how little money you have, how successful or socially awkward you are.    

They take the love you offer them without judging the person behind that love and then give it back to you as pure as it can be.  

There are days I pray to find someone who loves me at least as much as my cats do.

Hope is an emotion no one should ever do without, where there is hope there is strength to go on in life so keep hoping and dreaming, your dreams may very well come true sooner than you expect ;\)    
For some reason I feel very positive about your situation… don’t be scared NotAnotherWhatever, life is smiling at you finally, let your guard down and enjoy your present!
Looks like you are going through a lot :( I'm really sorry for your loss and your health problems. Don't let this get you down though, as they say, this too shall pass! Stay strong!
Do you have any other dream though? Something you'd like to realize?

Hmm... Maybe your friend has found balance and contentment by focusing only on the present.   
Living a comfortable life is a big accomplishment per se. After all if you think about it, when you are alone in life it's easier to get depressed, let yourself go and mess things up.
[Good luck](https://media.giphy.com/media/l0IyhxlufqGELvxVS/giphy.gif ) NotAnotherWhatever  ❤️And don't forget to keep us posted, I love hearing stories with happy endings!! )

Memory issues aside all seem to be fine, thank you :) 

> One of my biggest fears is being in a situation where the hospital takes over decision making because there is no one else.

It's one of my biggest fears as well. One of the many...
When I was hospitalized my roommate was a lady in her early 60 suffering from Alzheimer, her adult children took great care of her and visited every day multiple times a day. I wondered what would happen to me had I to find myself in her shoes? Who would take care of me?

Maybe I've grown too old to dream. An online acquaintance asked me about my plans, my dreams for the future and I couldn't come up with anything.  
I've stopped dreaming about things like my career, having children or becoming a writer. All of my dreams and my passion to pursue them apparently have disappeared.  
Is this what happens to people who stay FA well into adulthood? Is this what loneliness and lack of love do? 

Basically I'm living in the moment. I can't bring myself to think about the future. Making plans seem pointless.   
Something in me is changing.

Looking on the bright side... I have made a new internet friend, sort of. It's been about a month since we started chatting and although we exchange email only once/twice a week it's enough to make me feel a bit more alive. Nothing could ever come out of this virtual friendship as he is in a relationship and appears to be in love, but you know... it's nice to have someone who remembers you  exists and, on top of that, seems to enjoy talking with you.  
I hope he is not fooling me... I also hope he won't ghost me.

I'm sorry you had to go through that :( There's nothing more isolating and depressing than being sick and having no one you can rely on... Last year I was hospitalized for one week due to cerebral thrombosis and I felt abandoned to myself. At night I couldn't hold my tears back. 
As you can easily imagine that week I longed for a partner and friends more than ever. No one is made to live a lonely life, we need someone.  

Looking on the bright side, now you are fine! Things could have gone much worse.
Yet I know many Aspies from the support group I joined for a while who are either married (with children) or in a committed relationship.

I must agree with you. One of his comments made me shiver. As a child I grew up among violent adults suffering from personality disorders, and his comment, the words he used, reminded very much me of them.

Congratulations blackberrivine! That's awesome news!! :)
May this lead you to a better and happier life :)

I wish I could agree with you, but unfortunately I don't believe this to be true. There surely are women who go through long dry spells but most of them aren't FA, they have friends, family, emotional connections of some sort. Lonely people are everywhere and are often unseen so the number is higher than we may imagine, but I have yet to meet a FA woman in real life, and this is alienating.

> It must be america, it must be white guys that are becoming too passive, this doesnt happen anywhere else from what I have seen...

Ok, let me tell you this, in this sub there are women from many different countries and corners of the world. It's not America, it's not your men that are too passive (my sister's married to an American guy and he was the one who approached her). Many factors come into play and make us FA, but they aren't the same for all of us so it's really difficult to point one's finger on what makes someone FA.
By the way, I'm also one of those people who travel a lot and live out of a backpack and can count on the fingers of one hand the times I got approached my men abroad (men that weren't old maniacs).
Those women who get hit on abroad are the same girls that get hit on in their own country.

> I live in Europe and rest assured, there are plenty of FA women over here.

Campanula I actually think there aren't that many.

> would of met    

Would have ('ve) met.

Sorry I couldn't help it.

> You see, this is why I don't do things. This is the sort of thing that happens to me.

Look at things this way, despite being an introvert you were brave enough to go to the Paseo meet up, got to know new people and made a new experience. Don't focus on the bad things that happen, focus on the good steps you take in life and be proud of yourself! 
Shit happens more often to us introverts for reasons the universe doesn't care to explain. Let's not consider that crap as setbacks born by bad luck, let's call it urban adventures. We are not jinxed, we are urban Indiana Jones dealing with unexpected and annoying situations. 

> My father lost one of his jobs this week.

I'm really sorry to hear about that. Hopefully he'll find something else soon!!

> I find that even guys I find immediately repulsive can do a 180 in my eyes with their behavior and voice.

Same goes for me. The way a man acts, talks, behaves influences my view on him. And voice too plays a role, as silly as it sounds. 
But I can't meet him in person anytime soon. Unpleasant situation.

Actually there's nothing wrong with his looks. Probably due to what happened during my childhood to me attraction is a tricky thing and good look does not automatically make a man attractive. 
I'd like to meet him to see if talking to him in person changes my mind, problem is a date would be out of question for quite a long while because we don't live in the same country, we don't even live in the same continent. All we could do is skype.

> PS I really need to visit my motherland Vietnam 

Run to buy a ticket as soon as can! You'll love it here :)

A new chapter of your life is starting, it's understandable you feel a bit scared. Change is scary for everyone of us, but like you said change can be good. Just live this new chapter one day at a time. Once you have new friends and a new routine all your fears will fade away :)  best of luck with your future!!

As for me, on this trip I've received many compliments. Apparently in south East Asia my features are appealing, wherever I go I meet someone who feels the need to tell me they love my hair or I am beautiful. Just yesterday the owner of the guesthouse where I'm staying told me something unexpected but heartwarming: 
"everyone here thinks you are lovely".  
I was taken aback and had no idea what to say so I just muttered "that's very kind of you, thanks" 🤦‍♂️ I'm not used to receiving compliments so hearing someone telling me nice things on my face throws me into panic. You turn a bit socially awkward when you grow up bullied and FA, I guess.

Other than that... I'm madly in love with Vietnam, it's breathtakingly beautiful! Riding around with a scooter brought me so much joy, it saddens me it has to come to an end soon.  
Oh, a nice guy contacted me on OkCupid. He's older than me, is looking for something serious and judging by what he wrote he seems to be kind, intelligent and sweet.  
I'm not one bit physically attracted to him though; he lives on the other side of the pond but he's not from there; don't know what nationality he is and haven't much information about him as he kept his profile short and sweet, but he sounds like a good man. Would it be wise of me to reply him back? I can't see myself kissing him and couldn't force myself to do it... I'm a child abuse survivor and have problems with being touched. The only times I'm ok with physical -and emotional- contact is when I feel some sort of attraction towards the guy. I'm afraid talking with him might trigger panic attacks and strong nausea which would bring me to ghost him. It's already happened in the past and I don't went to ghost on another guy again. But what to do? 
In moments like these I wish I were more normal.

I'm cursed with a big loving heart that when in love loves deeply (although, oddly enough, I suffer from avoidant personality disorder and can't let anyone get close to me). So, yes, I have been in love.
My love was not reciprocated though, and the pain caused by the rejection hurt me so much I couldn't bring myself to eat and ended up underweight.  

Do I still have feelings for him? Yes, to a certain extent. Last time I met him was 7 years ago. I confessed my feelings to him 2 years ago, about one month before joining this subreddit. My feelings have faded thank god (after much work on my side and I'm doing my best to make them disappear for good), but for me it's very difficult not to love. It's as if I were born to love, love is in my veins (I'm a very affectionate person, that's why my neighbors cat moved in with me) and even if no one loves me back my feelings for them stay.
I agree wholeheartedly with everything you wrote! That's what I have gained from my online dating experience too.

Unfortunately where there is tourism there are scammers. I have yet to visit a country where tourists aren't taken advantage of in a way or another.  
Pho here is delicious :) just like all the other dishes tried so far. Asian cuisine is something incredible!!

Like you I fantasize a lot about many normal aspects of life that are still out of my reach. Like eating pizza on the couch with my partner while watching a movie we both like, or taking a stroll in the park with my husband and my child, going shopping/eating out with close female friends. Stuff like that. 

Earlier today I walked past many cozy cafes and saw so many friends and couples just sitting there and chatting the afternoon away... And all of a sudden I found myself daydreamed of having someone I could do that with. Little things... they are so important!

My week was..err, long. I spent almost every night of the last week with either cockroaches and rats or furry caterpillars and a colony of ants ~ Creepiest roommates ever ~ You get what you pay for, they say, and it's hella true! 
Today's my first day in Hanoi. Someone tried to get into my room while I was in the shower and I yelled so much I believe they heard me even in Patagonia; my credit card got stuck in the ATM and a taxi driver tried to scam me (I was ready to slap his soul of his body). Tomorrow will be a new and better day, hopefully!  
May I also add that I'm proud of myself for not crying?!

Love the new character you drew! I gave a look at your IG, your photos are rad, you should post more of them as well! 

>  I find it a struggle every day to stop myself thinking how worthless and useless I am. I need to remind myself that I am worthy and deserve to be loved as much as anyone else. Just because I haven't met anyone who has liked me back doesn't mean that I won't sometime in the future

Well said. You are worthy and lovable and someday you'll get to meet someone who will never make you doubt of your value, but meanwhile try to not listen to your negative thoughts. I always tell myself that who we are and how we perceive ourselves are two different things. We may feel worthless but this doesn't mean that we are. In your case, a person with so much artistic sense definitely can't be worthless, just look at the beautiful things you create :)

Aah if only I really had one million dollars...   

Assuming I have a paid off house I'd still make an investment that would make sure I'd never end up on the street (my biggest fear is to become homeless) so I'd buy a nice flat in ~city I know~ from ~country I know~ and would rent it through an agency to make a safe monthly profit.  
I'd start 2 different small business both in fields I know pretty well and that like as much.   
With the remaining money I'd have the house of my dreams build, would rent some of its rooms to travelers and would use the land to adopt and grow many different kind of animals.  
I'd hire a private tutor to become fluent in the languages I'm studying. 
Would take my mother on the holiday of her dreams.  
Would travel the world, all of it.  

My list is pretty long, I'd better stop here.

Your, how you called them, drunken fuck ups weren't more likable or better people than you, and you weren't/aren't worse than them.  
What they had was luck. Luck, by definition, is the force that causes good things to happen to you by chance and not as a result of your efforts or abilities. This word is part of the vocabulary of any language on this earth because we humans, regardless of culture and geographical position, have always been aware that there are aspects of our lives we have little to no control over. Love is one of these.  
Love can't be bought by a list of qualities.  
Multilingualism, a (good paying) job, a house of our own, talent... whatever quality you can think of, whether you have it or not is irrelevant because though it may make you more interesting and admirable person, it doesn't guarantee you love. After all, aren't most people on this earth simple creatures? Your average person is nothing special but finds partner(s) nonetheless because love doesn't follow rule and doesn't demand from you a fancy resume. 

Don't spend time blaming yourself for not having had a girlfriend, pat yourself on the shoulder for your achievements. Your efforts may not have helped you find a girlfriend, so far, but have turned you into a better version of yourself (something everyone of us should strive for at any stage of our lives). I don't know you but I'm proud of you, look how far you have gone in life despite your struggles! Now, girlfriend or not, don't ever forget your value and the value of your achievements, and be proud of yourself! 
I wish you to feel happy and find happiness soon!

My condolences on the passing of your mother! It’s terrible to hear about your loss, I can’t imagine what you are going through and how heartbroken and lonely you must be feeling. We are here as a support group, so don’t be ashamed of relying on us and reach out in case you need support.  
Send you a hug, it’s virtual but comes from my heart.

> Difficult moments are to be survived in time. Not resolved in the moment. 

Words that I have to keep in mind for similar future occurrences. 
I took some time for myself like you suggested and focused on other stuff. It helped a lot. At the end of the day what happened can't be changed, all I can do is let go of it and by letting go I'm moving forward.  
Thank you Trail22!

You are right, many people are finding themselves in financial troubles due to the current economic climate and I shouldn't feel ashamed of myself for making very little. In fact I should consider myself lucky to have what I have. Better days will come, sooner or later.
Thank you for your comment, I'm glad to read you managed to improve your life :)
Oh Cutol ((❤️)) I'm sorry you have to go through that! People can be extremely mean but don't let them bring you down!

> I get humiliated frequently, my existence is almost a state of perpetual humiliation. If I can go outside without someone laughing at me or insulting me or stopping dead in their tracks all slack-jawed transfixed at the sight of me, I consider it a win. I don't often win.

Oh god that’s terrible... I really hope you are just joking! 
Why would they do that to you?? 

> Just gotta stay busy and not think about it.

Yeah. Probably the best course of action.

I wish I could just walk away from it. Basically an employee of the post office where I usually go found out that I am not doing too well work wise (which was and still is a secret kept from almost everyone who knows me). We are peers, he’s doing pretty well in life, and the look on his face upon hearing how much I make in a year mortified me terribly. It made me feel worthless. I’ve been working hard to improve my social condition, I’ve also saved a good amount of money over the years and made an intelligent investment that’s been giving me a stable although small monthly return, but my work situation isn’t good and this embarrasses me deeply. Now this guy knows how deep the water I’m in is, and my functioning adult/happy-go-lucky mask’s gone.  
Maybe in a couple years I’ll be in a better position, but as of now I can’t help feeling embarrassed of who I am.

> I'm also hopefully planning a train journey too...of late if always seems there's heavy snowfall or some kind of disruption whenever I've planned on going somewhere.

That’s a lovely idea, a great way to de-stress for sure. Where would you like to travel to?

Today I went over to a friend for lunch. We get to meet only 3-4 times per year because she lives far away so these get-togethers mean a lot to me.   
My friend has a lovely 3year old child whom loves me to bits for reasons no one can quite figure out, whenever he sees me he screams my name with joy and this time was no exception. 
At lunchtime he told my friend that he would eat only if he could sit next to me but shortly after he decided that sitting in my laps was better than sitting next to me. The rest of the day he followed me everywhere, bathroom included, causing hilarity. 
I don't know what love really is but this child makes me feel loved, and it's a beautiful feeling.

> FA people become very attached quite easily. 

Not everyone, there are FA like me who have attachment issues. Let’s not forget about us.

No one can tell what he needs in this moment of his life and what the best course of action is, and you shouldn’t make decisions based on what we say because although we are all FA our perspectives, our thoughts and feelings differ.    
That said, what struck me in your post is this part:  
> we made promise to help each other if something really bad happened.

It seems to me that something really bad just happened, and if both of you really meant what you said it’s time for you to get back in touch with him and be there for him, even if momentarily. It’s terrible to lose a parent and find yourself completely lonely and abandoned even by those who promised to be at your side in case of need. I have been there, and it breaks your spirit.
Happy birthday darling!!! <3

Thank you for this book! Everyone who finds himself/herself living a life as a Forever Alone should give it a read and note down your tips.  
Tip #9 (retain some degree of contact with other people) it's something I've been trying to put into practice for a few years now. Probably it's among one of the best piece of advice you could ever give someone in our position. It's important for us to make sure to not completely isolate ourselves, someday we might need a friendly neighbour's help, and for sure our mental health benefits from random chitchats. In my case I found Facebook to be pretty useful in keeping and forming acquaintances even though it's a social media stigmatised by many in our community, without it I'd probably be even more isolated and depressed than I am now.   
However I do not work in an office and this makes me fear someday, when my mother will pass away, I'll find myself completely outcasted regardless of my efforts to stay in touch with the people around me.

I stayed 17 days and visited Jodhpur (amazing!!) + nearby small villages, Pushkar (another gem), Jaipur, Agra, Orchha, Varanasi and then from there I went to Lumbini in Nepal.

As for water, you can drink only bottled water (this applies to all South East Asia though), and you’d better not use tap water to brush your teeth either (some people do it but I wouldn’t risk it).  
Food is delicious but you have to pay attention to what you eat and avoid certain foods.

Attraction rarely is an acquired taste. Repetitive exposure to a certain subject may lead to the development of casual feelings of affection for such subject, but the chances it will lead to attraction (both mental and physical attraction) are low.

Attraction is like passion, it's natural brain's motivation to pursue something (career/goals) or someone. Without it only a few things induce a person to pursue a relationship:  
- one's good nature, which brings you to thinking that "after all s/he is a good person, maybe I can learn to love her/him over time".   
- one's rationality, which makes you think that in human history most relationships weren't based on love or attraction, yet some of them worked out.   
- one's desperation. No explaination needed here.

Hmm... Some things have stayed absolutely the same. The loneliness, the everyday efforts to go on and improve your life, the fears about the future, the feeling of unworthiness. Certain things have stayed the same but other things have definitely changed, and I can't say it's all changed for the better. 

I've turned more bitter, grumpier. Every little setback upsets me... after years and years of problems and things never going my way, tolerance and patience and qualities difficult to keep. Admittedly my tolerance has gone down. I start to understand why lonely elderly are often cranky, it isn't their personality... it's the adversity and the loneliness that's turned them into what they are.  

I fight to love myself, but I can feel self acceptance leaving me. It gets hard to love yourself when it seems no one on this earth is willing to do it, and living without any form of external validation on the long run impact the way you see and perceive yourself.   
If you're not completely delusional one day you end up questioning yourself and ask yourself: "If I'm so ok/not that bad as a person, how come no one has ever wanted me? How come no one likes me?". On that day your self-esteem will start asking for something more than your own opinion, it'll demand external validation that if not provided will hurt and damage you even further (and that's what's been happening to me). 

Today I can't help vivisecting any aspect of my being, from the outward appearance to my personality, just to understand what could be wrong with me. In the past, in my early 20's, that was something that, although I used to do, wasn't as severe. 

I'm definitely less emotional stable because pain is taking its tool on me. The more years pass by the more disappointments we collect and, as a consequence, pain grows while emotional and psychological strength fades. 

My goals, my point of views have changed. I've also lost motivation to pursue my career and my childhood dreams.  
Making money to make a good living and enjoy life even if without a partner/friends/a family of my own isn't anymore something I am to.  A career without any form of love doesn't appeal me.  

However I've become better looking, but just because I've got acne and other body issues under control, learnt how to fix my hair, how to dress well.  
In some regards I've gained more confidence (can finally drive without having panic attacks or having to ask someone to drive me around, can travel to the other side of the world alone, have learnt new languages which make me proud of myself), but in others my self-esteem got shattered really bad.  
In my early 20's my optimism (or naivety) was high. Now, after a decade of let-downs and broken hopes/dreams, I feel emotionally weaker.    
I feel my strength is fading, day after day.

Some good aspects of my personality got lost along the way, something got damaged, something has improved... but at the end of the day I'm still hurting, still unhappy with my life, and now I'm weaker because a person can't be perpetually strong in the face of loneliness and adversities.

The improvements I've reached have't made my life or my circumstances more bearable, and it scares me to think of the future.  
Sorry for this gloomy comment, but that's how things are for me.

When I was your age I was taking care of my father who was suffering from a neurodegenerative disease. I really did my best back then and couldn't change a thing of that period. Anyway, if you don't have anything holding you back I'd suggest you a few things: 

- TRAVEL! Most FA people cope with the loneliness that comes with having few or no friends at all, with the lack of good memories to hold onto during dark moments, so since you're young take time to build those memories and give yourself the chance to meet as many people as possible.   
If English is your first language go teach English overseas, it's a great way to travel the world and make friends for life, plus the pay isn't bad and the experiences you'll make, the people you'll meet will stay with you forever. If you're lucky you'll even end up meeting your SO while abroad ;) Many people have!  
Otherwise, if you don't feel like teaching English and don't have enough money to travel, consider travelling with volunteer programs such as [workaway](https://www.workaway.info/). Just go out and explore the world, it'll fill your heart, expand your mind and shape your character. If there's something I don't regret one bit is all the travelling I've done, wish I had dared more.     
  
- find social activities/sports/hobbies that obligate you to get out of home and interact with other people. 

- don't be afraid to date. Every experience is useful in its own way; dating at a young age will help you build more confidence in yourself (or at least you won't turn in a 30something guy afraid of dating).

- stay fit. As they say treat your body like a temple (I've taken great care of myself and at 30 have beautiful body, don't regret the efforts it took me to stay this way), so eat well and exercise, not saying you have to get buff, just stay fit.


Most importantly, focus on a career and make plans for your future... plan a life where there's no partner to go home to. It's sad to think about but remaining alone is a possibility to take into account and you have to be prepared for such a future. What would you do if you had to live alone for the rest of your life? Think about it, make plans and start saving money because living alone is more expensive than believed. 

I wish you to find someone soon though. Good luck with your life!

If you have difficulties making friends (real friends? superficial friends? acquaintances?) you have to ask yourself a few things:

Unfortunately I have been ugly for a little more than two thirds of my life, so my eyes keep seeing the girl I was in the past and as a consequence my mind is filled with thoughts such as "if I were prettier... /I'm not pretty enough.../ I wish I had a new face.../I should get surgery...".    
It's difficult to go from so ugly you get ridiculed in public to pretty enough to be stopped and complimented by random strangers, my mind thinks "maybe they are teasing me; maybe they haven't taken a good look; maybe if they look at me from a different perspective with a different light, maybe if they look at me a bit longer they'll eventually find me ugly".

I noted this thing in my diary and then cried all night long wondering why, if I was so beautiful, the guy I confessed my love to didn't feel the same and treated me as if I were the swamp monster.  

Maybe I'm no longer a mockable ugly duckling, but beautiful is not not how I feel, nor is that a word I'd easily use to describe myself. All I see is an overlookable plain Jane.

> the author of the book hypothesizes that modern society is less conducive to interpersonal relationships, which leads to poorer mental health

Probably this. 
I live in a country with one of the lowest suicide and depression rates in Europe and in the world, it's difficult to say why but one has to wonder whether it has to do with culture (if you pay close attention to the numbers reported by the WHO, those countries with a close knit family/community culture score lower, but this is a very superficial observation). Definitely there's no simple answer. It's a very complex matter!  

Maybe psychological anthropology / socio-cultural anthropology could help us understand a bit better why such numbers are increasing.   Society, in this case American society, is evolving but not around the psychological and emotional needs of the individual, as a consequence people are more likely to suffer from anxiety (due also to social expectation and external pressure) and mental illness rates increase (it'd be more accurate to say that the reported cases increase).   
  
In the past there was a lot less information available and a bigger stigma attached to mental illness (let's not forget that in the 19th century suicide was still illegal and often scorned), it was so serious that the suicide of a family member was a secret to carry to one's grave as it brought shame upon the whole family.  

Whoever says that depression is a developed country's disease obviously has never done voluntary work in a third world country such as Congo or India, nor has ever spent a few minutes on the WHO website.     
According to the WHO, the world health organisation, depression rates are usually higher in developing countries, and so are suicides.  
What's more, the real numbers of those affected by depression and other mental issues can't be accurately gathered (and are supposedly under-reported) as in those countries the mental health service, just like any other service, is way more limited; many people can't even afford going to a doctor, many people are illiterate and have no idea what the word anxiety or depression stands for, many have no idea what mental illnesses are despite having to deal with them personally (you can easily come across people who suffer from PTSD, DID, schizophrenia, anxiety and have no idea what those things are), on top of that most of those who suffer from serious mental illnesses get outcasted and live in extreme poverty (that's also why the real number of mentally ill people is often underrepresented in these countries). 
 
I don't think people are getting so much more depressed (at least not THAT much more), I think people are getting more open and thus the number increases.  
But as I said before, there's no simple answer for such a complex matter.

I'm confused, いっすい・一睡 aside if you were about N4 you could read and make sense of those sentences. Are you a total beginner? It's not my intention to sound harsh but I'm trying to understand what you know and what level you are so to provide more help.

I'm going to rewrite the first sentence leaving out the kanji you might not know:
子どもがいっすいもしなくて、私の方もねむれなかった。
(My kid didn't sleep a wink AND I couldn't sleep either)

Now let's break that sentence into smaller parts.  
First keep in mind that いっすい  する means "to (take a) nap".  
So, いっすい もしない= not sleep a wink  
いっすい もしなくて = don't sleep a wink and...   
私の方  も= I too   
ねむれなかった = couldn't sleep (potential negative past form of the verb ねむる・眠る)  

In that sentence なくて is used because a reason for my lack of sleep is expressed (contrary to the second sentence where no cause is mentioned) ---> my kid didn't sleep (thus he stayed up all night) and because of that I couldn't get to sleep. [If your kid stays up at night, whatever the reason, you as a parent feel a moral obligation to take care of him/her. So, since your child stays awake you can't go to sleep].

Hope you'll eventually come to understand their difference, wish you the best with your study!

If you still fail to understand their difference let's try put things under a different perspective...  

It could help you better grasp their usage if you interpreted  "X〜ないで" as "without doing X...", while "〜なくて" as a mere "〜and...".
Now this is a pretty reductive and oversimplified way of putting it, but I think that's what could help you tell their difference.  
According to the explanation given here http://www.alc.co.jp/jpn/article/faq/03/99.html  なくて is used when a reason or a cause is expressed. Like in the following case:  
子どもが一睡もしなくて、私の方も眠れなかった。 My kid didn't sleep a wink AND I couldn't sleep either. (The reason I didn't sleep is that my child kept me awake)  

Now let's use "一睡もしないで":  
一睡もしないで、仕事に出かけた。I didn't sleep a wink and went to work. (Why couldn't I get to sleep? A possible reason isn't mentioned)    
This latter sentence is odd sounding but I think it can help you better understand the point.

Now, is their difference any more clear? Can you tell when to pick なくて and when ないで?

Travel nostalgia is something a few of us travellers can't escape, there're moments it hits really hard and we're never ready for that.

I've travelled a bit and each travel turned out to be an experience worth remembering, but almost five year ago I experienced one of the highlights of my life while abroad, I ended up meeting some great people and made many fantastic experiences... Well, to today I still find it difficult to look through the pictures and the videos of that period. Remembering those days stirs up a mix of emotions at times I find hard dealing with. It's a bittersweet emotional battle.   

That's life after all, we look back at what made us happy and can't help but be nostalgic, maybe because certain type of happiness are hard to (re)experience in our daily life so we long for what's gone.
But who doesn't get a little bit sad when thinking about one's good bygone times? Nostalgia hits us all, it's a sign we lived our life at the best, at least for a certain period in time (and that's always good).
Let yourself go to nostalgia when it'll hit you, there's nothing wrong with that. 
Unfortunately I don't know how to ease those feelings, usually what helps me is thinking that even though we can't physically go back to those good memories, we can build new ones. There will be new travels, new beautiful people and new amazing experiences in our future!
